evidence_review: Numerical findings supplied in the operator's 2026-10-13 primary-abstract audit; verify against the linked PubMed abstract before apply. No secondary source or model was used.
abstract: Design: Pragmatic randomized controlled trial. Participants: 7294 surgical patients with cognitive impairment were randomized. Interventions: AI-driven perioperative clinical decision support versus routine care. Primary outcome: Postoperative delirium within seven postoperative days. Results: Delirium assessments were documented in 1255 patients. In those assessed, delirium occurred in 225/641 (35.1%) in the intervention group versus 201/614 (32.7%) in the control group, P=.37; a statistically significant difference was not demonstrated. Adherence to best practices showed no significant differences (all P>.05). Limitations: Missing delirium assessments in most randomized patients limit interpretation; absence of statistical significance is not proof of no effect. Conclusions: These data do not establish a delirium-prevention benefit.
